user.title: Solar Energy Management Setup

data.observer_mode: Test mode (read-only — do not control hardware)

data_description.observer_mode: Leave OFF for a normal install. Turn ON only on a test/staging Home Assistant that mirrors a production instance, so SEM never sends commands to KEBA, the inverter, or any switches. You can change this any time later in the Configuration tab → Advanced.

ev_charger.title: EV Charger
ev_charger.description: SEM auto-detected your EV charger from the Home Assistant entity registry. Review the entries below and click **Submit** — there is usually nothing to change. Optional fields can be left blank.

data.ev_connected_sensor: 🔌 EV Connected Status — vehicle plug connection
data.ev_charging_sensor: ⚡ EV Charging Active — current charging state
data.ev_charging_power_sensor: 🚗 EV Charging Power — power delivered to vehicle (W)
data.ev_total_energy_sensor: 🔋 EV Total Energy — cumulative energy delivered (kWh)
data.ev_current_control_entity: Number Entity for Current Control (Wallbox-style chargers)

data_description.ev_connected_sensor: Binary sensor that reports whether the vehicle plug is currently connected. Auto-detected from KEBA / Easee / Wallbox / go-eCharger / Zaptec / ChargePoint / Heidelberg.
data_description.ev_charging_sensor: Binary sensor that reports whether SEM should consider charging active. Auto-detected from your charger integration.
data_description.ev_charging_power_sensor: Numeric sensor (W) reporting how much power is currently flowing into the vehicle. Auto-detected from your charger integration.
data_description.ev_charger_service: Home Assistant service called to set the charging current (e.g. keba.set_current, easee.set_charger_max_limit). Auto-filled for KEBA. Leave blank for chargers controlled via a number entity.
data_description.ev_charger_service_entity_id: Entity ID passed as the target of the service call. Auto-filled when needed; leave blank if the service is global.
data_description.ev_current_sensor: Optional. Numeric sensor (A) reporting the actual charging current. Used for diagnostics.
data_description.ev_total_energy_sensor: Optional. Cumulative kWh counter for energy delivered to the vehicle. Used for accurate session tracking.
data_description.ev_current_control_entity: Number entity SEM writes to so it can change the charging current (e.g. number.wallbox_charging_current). Use this for chargers that expose a number entity instead of a service call. Leave blank if you fill in the Service path below.

data.generate_dashboard_on_install: Generate the SEM dashboard now (restarts HA)

data_description.generate_dashboard_on_install: When enabled, SEM creates the Lovelace dashboard immediately after this step finishes and then restarts Home Assistant ~5 s later so the new dashboard becomes visible. data_description.diagram_style: Choose which system diagram card to use on the Home tab. 'SEM' uses the built-in animated diagram. 'K-Flow' uses the K-Flow HACS card (must be installed separately).
data_description.battery_capacity_kwh: Total usable capacity of your home battery (NOT the EV) in kWh. Used by the forecast-driven charging strategy to estimate how much battery can bridge a solar deficit. Check your inverter spec.

ev_charger.title: EV Charger
ev_charger.description:
Tip: most settings now live on the SEM dashboard → Configuration tab (colorful, live). This flow remains for headless setups and entity wiring.

Review and update your EV charger entity mappings. The Vehicle SOC fields are only used if you provide a Vehicle Battery SOC sensor.

data_description.ev_connected_sensor: Binary sensor that reports whether the vehicle plug is connected.
data_description.ev_charging_sensor: Binary sensor that reports whether the EV is actively charging.
data_description.ev_charging_power_sensor: Numeric sensor (W) reporting power currently flowing into the vehicle.
data_description.ev_charger_service: HA service called to set the charging current. Leave blank for number-entity chargers.
data_description.ev_charger_service_entity_id: Entity ID passed as the service call target. Leave blank if not needed.
data_description.ev_total_energy_sensor: Optional cumulative kWh counter for energy delivered to the vehicle.
data_description.vehicle_soc_entity: Optional sensor reporting the vehicle's current state of charge (0–100%).
data_description.ev_battery_capacity_kwh: Total usable capacity of the EV battery in kWh. Used to estimate SOC and charge time.
data_description.ev_charger_efficiency: Share of the metered AC energy that reaches the battery. Lower it if the SOC estimate runs ahead of the car. Typically 85-95%, less on single-phase or in cold weather.
data_description.ev_target_soc: SEM stops treating the car as needing charge once it reaches this. It is a definition of "full", not a limit on charging.
data_description.daily_ev_target_max: Solar surplus stops charging here. This is a ceiling, not a goal — leave it at full to charge freely from the sun.
data_description.ev_target_soc_max: Solar surplus stops charging here. This is a ceiling, not a goal — leave at 100% to charge freely from the sun.
data_description.vehicle_range_entity: Optional real range sensor. Otherwise range is estimated from SOC × capacity × efficiency.
data_description.ev_kwh_per_100km: Used to estimate driving range when no range sensor is configured.

heat_pump.title: Heat Pump
heat_pump.description:
Configure your heat pump for solar surplus boost. Two control paths are supported:
• **SG-Ready** — set both relay entities (Viessmann, Stiebel Eltron, Vaillant).
• **Climate-only** — set just the climate entity (Nibe, Mitsubishi, Daikin and any HA-controlled heat pump without SG-Ready relays).
Both paths can also be combined. Leave all empty to skip.

data.heat_pump_sg_ready_service_data: SG-Ready service data (JSON; placeholders state, relay1, relay2)

data_description.heat_pump_relay1_entity: Switch entity for SG-Ready relay 1 (normal operation signal). Set together with relay 2 for SG-Ready protocol.
data_description.heat_pump_relay2_entity: Switch entity for SG-Ready relay 2 (surplus boost signal). Set together with relay 1 for SG-Ready protocol.
data_description.heat_pump_invert_sg_ready: Enable only if your heat pump's SG-Ready contacts are wired normally-closed (NC). SEM drives the standard SG-Ready truth table; if boost blocks the pump (and vice-versa), turn this on to flip both relays.
data_description.heat_pump_climate_entity: Climate entity used to raise the setpoint during solar surplus. Sufficient on its own for climate-only mode (no relays needed).
data_description.heat_pump_power_sensor: Optional sensor (W) reporting the heat pump's current power consumption.
data_description.heat_pump_boost_offset: Degrees Celsius added to the normal setpoint during a solar surplus boost.
data_description.heat_pump_max_setpoint: Upper temperature limit (°C) SEM will set during a boost cycle.
data_description.heat_pump_priority: Surplus distribution priority relative to other devices. Lower numbers are served first.

data_description.action: Choose whether to add a new charger, edit an existing one, or remove one.

ev_charger_add.title: Add EV Charger
ev_charger_add.description:
Configure a new EV charger. SEM will distribute surplus power across chargers by priority.

For current control, use EITHER the number entity (Wallbox, go-eCharger) OR the service (KEBA). Leave the other blank.

data_description.charger_name: Friendly name for this charger shown in the dashboard (e.g. 'Garage' or 'Carport').
data_description.ev_connected_sensor: Binary sensor that reports whether a vehicle is plugged into this charger.
data_description.ev_charging_sensor: Binary sensor that reports whether this charger is actively delivering power.
data_description.ev_charging_power_sensor: Numeric sensor (W) reporting power delivered by this charger.
data_description.ev_current_control_entity: Number entity used to set the charging current (A). Use for Wallbox, go-eCharger, and similar chargers.
data_description.ev_charger_service: HA service used to set the charging current (e.g. keba.set_current). Use for KEBA or Easee.
data_description.ev_charger_service_entity_id: Entity ID passed as the target of the service call. Leave blank if not needed.
data_description.ev_start_stop_entity: Switch or button that physically starts/stops charging. Set this when dropping to 0 A does not release the charger (Smart EVSE, some OCPP boxes) — SEM opens it instead of leaving the contactor cycling.
data_description.ev_current_sensor: Sensor reporting the current the charger is actually offering (A). Lets SEM verify a command landed instead of assuming it did.
data_description.ev_charge_mode_entity: Select entity SEM switches to start/stop charging on boxes that need a mode change rather than a current of 0 A (go-e, Ohme, some OCPP).
data_description.ev_charge_mode_start: The option SEM selects to START charging (e.g. "Instant Charging", "2"). Must match the select's option exactly.
data_description.ev_charge_mode_stop: The option SEM selects to STOP charging. Leave blank if stopping is done by the start/stop entity or by setting 0 A.
data_description.ev_surplus_priority: Surplus allocation order across multiple chargers. Lower number = higher priority.
data_description.daily_ev_target_max: Solar surplus stops charging here. This is a ceiling, not a goal — leave it at full to charge freely from the sun.
data_description.ev_target_soc_max: Solar surplus stops charging here. This is a ceiling, not a goal — leave at 100% to charge freely from the sun.
data_description.daily_ev_target: SEM tops up from the grid overnight so the car has at least this much by morning. This is a floor, not a limit — sunshine can add more. 0 = never use the grid.
data_description.vehicle_soc_entity: Optional sensor reporting the vehicle's current state of charge (0–100%).
data_description.vehicle_range_entity: Optional real range sensor. Otherwise range is estimated from SOC × capacity × efficiency.
data_description.ev_kwh_per_100km: Used to estimate driving range when no range sensor is configured.
data_description.ev_target_soc: SEM stops treating the car as needing charge once it reaches this. It is a definition of "full", not a limit on charging.
data_description.ev_battery_capacity_kwh: Total usable capacity of the EV battery in kWh. Used to estimate SOC and charge time.
data_description.initial_current: Charge current SEM begins with before ramping to match available surplus.
data_description.ev_min_current: Below this SEM pauses charging instead of dropping the current further.
data_description.ev_phase_switch_entity: Select/number/switch that changes the charger between 1- and 3-phase charging (go-e 'psm', KEBA X-series, openWB). SEM only observes and validates it for now — automatic switching comes in a later release.
data_description.ev_phase_switch_value_1p: What to write to the phase-switch entity for 1-phase charging — a select's option name, a number's value, or on/off. Required for select entities; number defaults to 1, switch to off.
data_description.ev_phase_switch_value_3p: What to write to the phase-switch entity for 3-phase charging — a select's option name, a number's value, or on/off. Required for select entities; number defaults to 3, switch to on.
data_description.ev_phase_switching_enabled: Off by default while the 1/3-phase model is reworked (it paused chargers that never resumed on some brands). Turn on to test it on your charger.

settings.title: Battery & SOC Zones
settings.description: Configure the 4-zone SOC strategy. Zone 1 (< Priority): battery first. Zone 2 (Priority–Buffer): surplus only. Zone 3 (Buffer–Auto-start): battery assists EV. Zone 4 (≥ Auto-start): full battery assist.

data.min_solar_power: Minimum solar power — raw PV production (W)
data.battery_discharge_protection_enabled: Enable battery discharge protection at night

data_description.update_interval: How often the coordinator reads sensors and adjusts hardware. 10 s gives the most accurate energy integration; values above 30 s will under-count energy. Range 10–60 s.
data_description.battery_priority_soc: Zone 1 → Zone 2 boundary. Below this SOC all solar goes to the battery and the EV is blocked. Default 30 %. The four-zone strategy (Architecture docs) needs this LOW (5–60 %) — do NOT confuse with the legacy 3-zone meaning where this was a high target.
data_description.battery_buffer_soc: Zone 2 → Zone 3 boundary. Above this SOC the battery may discharge to bridge solar deficits while charging the EV. Default 70 %.
data_description.battery_auto_start_soc: Zone 3 → Zone 4 boundary. Above this SOC the EV can start charging even with no solar surplus, drawing from the battery. Default 90 %.
data_description.min_solar_power: Raw PV-production floor — the panel output below which 'solar is up' is false: solar_only won't start and the deep-deficit guard treats it as darkness (so charging stops quickly instead of bridging on grid). This is RAW production, NOT surplus — contrast 'Battery assist minimum solar surplus' (solar − home), which decides when the home battery may help. Default 1000 W; keep below the EV charger's hardware minimum (~4140 W 3-phase, ~1380 W 1-phase).
data_description.daily_ev_target: SEM tops up from the grid overnight so the car has at least this much by morning. This is a floor, not a limit — sunshine can add more. 0 = never use the grid.
data_description.battery_assist_max_power: Maximum power the home battery can discharge to assist the EV in Zone 3/4. Default 4500 W.
data_description.battery_assist_min_surplus: Minimum real solar surplus before the home battery may help charge the EV — in any charging mode. Below this the battery is reserved for the house (the car draws from grid + solar). Default 1200 W. Set to 0 to let the battery support the EV everywhere, including overnight.
data_description.battery_capacity_kwh: Total usable home battery capacity (NOT the EV battery — that's a separate field on the EV step). Used by the forecast-driven charging strategy.
data_description.battery_discharge_protection_enabled: When ON, SEM caps the inverter's discharge limit during night EV charging so the home battery only powers the house (not the EV).
data_description.battery_max_discharge_power: Hard upper limit on battery discharge enforced by the protection feature.
data_description.electricity_import_rate: Day / flat tariff (CHF/kWh, incl. VAT). Used for cost tracking.
data_description.electricity_off_peak_rate: Night tariff (CHF/kWh). Set equal to import rate if you don't have a dual tariff.
data_description.electricity_export_rate: Feed-in rate paid by the utility (CHF/kWh).
data_description.demand_charge_rate: Monthly demand charge per kW of peak (CHF/kW/month). Set to 0 if your contract has no demand charge.
data_description.observer_mode: When ON, SEM monitors and calculates everything but never sends a service call to hardware. Use on a test/staging HA mirroring a production install.
data_description.smart_night_charging: When ON, SEM intelligently skips or reduces night charging based on estimated EV SOC, solar forecast, temperature-adjusted consumption prediction, and learned driving patterns.
data_description.battery_discharge_control_entity: Number entity that controls the inverter's discharge power limit (e.g. number.batteries_maximale_entladeleistung on Huawei). Auto-detected on install; override here if needed.
data_description.hot_water_solar_target: Target temperature (°C) for solar-assisted hot water heating. SEM boosts the boiler when surplus is available.
data_description.legionella_target_temp: Temperature (°C) the hot water system must reach during a legionella disinfection cycle.
data_description.legionella_interval_hours: Maximum hours between legionella disinfection cycles before SEM forces a heat-up.
data_description.diagram_style: Choose which system diagram card to use on the Home tab. 'SEM' uses the built-in animated diagram. 'K-Flow' uses the K-Flow HACS card (must be installed separately). Re-run the generate_dashboard service after changing.
data_description.grid_sign_invert: Turn ON only if grid import shows as a positive value (e.g. Enphase). SEM's convention is negative = import; this negates the raw reading and bypasses sign auto-detection.
data_description.battery_operating_mode_entity: The inverter's operating-policy selector (e.g. Huawei's 'Working mode'). SEM only READS it: the mode is shown beside the battery evidence, and a one-time repair warns when it is not the self-consumption mode SEM's planning assumes. SEM never changes it. Leave empty to disable the watch.

settings_ev.title: EV Charging & Solar
settings_ev.description: Configure EV charging targets and solar thresholds.

data.smart_night_charging: Reduce night target based on tomorrow's forecast
data.minimum_solar_power: Minimum solar power to start EV charging (W)

data_description.daily_ev_target: SEM tops up from the grid overnight so the car has at least this much by morning. This is a floor, not a limit — sunshine can add more. 0 = never use the grid.
data_description.observer_mode: When ON, SEM monitors everything but never sends commands to hardware.
data_description.smart_night_charging: When ON, SEM reduces the night charge target when tomorrow's solar forecast is sufficient.
data_description.minimum_solar_power: Minimum surplus solar power (W) required before SEM starts solar EV charging.
data_description.curtailment_probe_enabled: When your inverter caps grid export (e.g. at negative prices), production clamps to consumption and real solar stays invisible. Opt-in: SEM briefly starts the EV at minimum amps and keeps charging only if production rises to follow.
data_description.export_limit_entity: Your inverter's export-limit entity (auto-detected for Huawei, GoodWe, SolaX, Victron and others when empty). Sharpens curtailment detection and prevents unnecessary probes.

settings_tariff.title: Tariff & Advanced
settings_tariff.description: Choose your tariff mode: **Static** for fixed rates, **Dynamic** for real-time pricing (Tibber, Nordpool, aWATTar, Amber Electric, Octopus Energy), or **Calendar** for time-based HT/NT schedules. SEM auto-detects your provider — if detection fails (e.g. renamed integration), select the entities manually.

data.dynamic_forecast_entity: Price forecast entity (optional, auto-detected if empty)
data.dynamic_feedin_entity: Feed-in price entity (optional, for dynamic export rate)
data.grid_import_power_entity: Grid import power sensor (optional, auto-detected from Energy Dashboard)
data.grid_export_power_entity: Grid export power sensor (optional, auto-detected from Energy Dashboard)

data_description.tariff_mode: Choose 'Static' for fixed rates, 'Dynamic' for real-time pricing, or 'Calendar' for time-of-use schedules.
data_description.dynamic_tariff_entity: Sensor providing the current electricity import price. Auto-detected from Tibber, Nordpool, etc.
data_description.dynamic_forecast_entity: Optional sensor with hourly price forecasts used for smart scheduling.
data_description.dynamic_feedin_entity: Optional sensor providing the current feed-in / export price for dynamic export rate.
data_description.electricity_import_rate: Day/flat import rate (currency/kWh incl. VAT). Used as fallback when dynamic pricing is unavailable.
data_description.grid_import_surcharge: Optional total variable network-owner fee added to every imported kWh. May combine electricity transfer and energy tax. Use only when the dynamic price entity excludes these fees. No fixed subscription; does not affect export.
data_description.electricity_off_peak_rate: Night/off-peak import rate (currency/kWh). Set equal to import rate if you have a flat tariff.
data_description.electricity_export_rate: Feed-in rate paid by the utility (currency/kWh).
data_description.demand_charge_rate: Monthly peak-demand charge (currency/kW/month). Set to 0 if your contract has none.
data_description.update_interval: How often SEM reads sensors and adjusts hardware (seconds). Range 10–60 s.
data_description.grid_import_power_entity: Optional sensor (W) for grid import power. Auto-detected from the Energy Dashboard; override here if needed.
data_description.grid_export_power_entity: Optional sensor (W) for grid export power. Auto-detected from the Energy Dashboard; override here if needed.
data_description.tariff_classification_mode: Percentile buckets prices relative to today's range (recommended). Static uses fixed cheap/expensive thresholds.
data_description.solar_forecast_source: Which forecast integration SEM reads. Auto-detect prefers Solcast, then Forecast.Solar, then Open-Meteo — pick one explicitly if you run several side by side.

data.peak_slot_guard_enabled: Enforce the limit within each 15-minute slot

data_description.load_management_enabled: Enable/disable SEM's automatic load-shedding to stay under your grid peak limit.
data_description.peak_limit_unlimited: Turn peak management off entirely: SEM stops sizing loads against the target peak limit and never sheds to defend it. Only for connections large enough that no household load can threaten them. This is separate from Enable Load Management, which stops the shedding but keeps the limit as a sizing ceiling.
data_description.target_peak_limit: Maximum grid power (kW) before SEM starts shedding controllable loads.
data_description.warning_peak_level: Power level (kW) at which SEM issues a warning before taking action. Must be below the target peak limit.
data_description.emergency_peak_level: Power level (kW) at which SEM aggressively sheds loads to avoid demand charges. Must be above the target peak limit.
data_description.vehicle_soc_entity: Optional sensor reporting the vehicle's current state of charge (0–100%).
data_description.ev_battery_capacity_kwh: Total usable capacity of the EV battery in kWh.
data_description.ev_target_soc: SEM stops treating the car as needing charge once it reaches this. It is a definition of "full", not a limit on charging.
data_description.peak_slot_guard_enabled: Preventive guard: bounds every command SEM sends — EV offers, battery grid-charging, cheap-hour load starts — by the current billing slot's remaining budget, before the meter records a peak. Off keeps only the reactive shedding (the pre-guard behaviour).

data_description.enable_charger_notifications: Enable/disable persistent notification banners on the charger status card.
data_description.enable_mobile_notifications: Enable/disable push notifications sent to your mobile device.
data_description.mobile_notification_service: HA notify service for mobile push (e.g. notify.mobile_app_your_phone).
data_description.vehicle_soc_entity: Optional sensor reporting the vehicle's current state of charge (0–100%).
data_description.ev_battery_capacity_kwh: Total usable capacity of the EV battery in kWh.
data_description.ev_target_soc: SEM stops treating the car as needing charge once it reaches this. It is a definition of "full", not a limit on charging.

battery_scheduler.description: Configure forecast-aware grid-to-battery charging during cheap hours
battery_scheduler.title: Battery Charge Scheduler

data_description.battery_charge_platform: Which inverter SEM commands for scheduled grid charging. Choose Deye to reveal the Deye wiring step.
data_description.battery_replan_interval_min: How often the charge schedule is recomputed against the latest forecast and prices.
data_description.battery_prefer_consecutive_window: On keeps the cheap hours in one block (fewer start/stop cycles); off picks the individual cheapest hours even if scattered.
data_description.battery_charge_power_limit_entity: The inverter's max-charge-power number that charge pacing writes to (e.g. Huawei's 'Maximum charging power'). Leave empty to keep pacing advisory-only.
data_description.inverter_ac_limit_w: Your inverter's maximum AC output in watts. Charge pacing opens its cap wherever solar would exceed this, so clipped sun is captured. 0 = not set.

pv_naming.title: Name your PV strings

settings_phase_guard_topology.title: Electrical topology
settings_phase_guard_topology.description: Choose how the house load is supplied. In a hybrid installation, the grid and the inverter Load/EPS/Backup output can feed the house at the same time. The load inside the house can therefore be higher than the current through the main fuse. SEM monitors the two paths independently. Enforcement is opt-in; verify the readings in Observer Mode before enabling EV control.

For a three-phase supply, select a complete L1-L3 direct RMS-current family when available; otherwise grid current is calculated from absolute power divided by voltage. For a hybrid Load/EPS lane, select non-negative RMS current sensors for the configured phases. Missing, stale, invalid or negative required readings fail closed. sensor_unavailable.title: Sensor unavailable
sensor_unavailable.description: The sensor `{entity_id}` ({friendly_name}) has been unavailable for {minutes}+ minutes. SEM cannot include it in calculations until it recovers. Check the upstream integration (Huawei modbus / Solcast / Forecast.Solar / your inverter network). This issue clears automatically when the sensor next reports a valid value.

sensor_stale.title: Sensor frozen
sensor_stale.description: The sensor `{entity_id}` ({friendly_name}) still reports as available but has not updated in {minutes}+ minutes — it appears frozen. SEM is using its stale value in the energy balance and sign detection, which can distort your figures. Check the upstream integration (Huawei modbus / Growatt cloud / your inverter network). This issue clears automatically when the sensor next updates.

confirm.title: Report this to SEM
confirm.description:
SEM's last 3+ current commands to **{name}** were rejected: `{error}`. The charger is NOT under SEM control right now — it will keep doing whatever it was last told (including charging at full power in off mode). Most common causes: the charger's control entity was renamed by an upstream integration update, or `ev_charger_service` points at a service with a different parameter schema. Check the charger's control entity / service in the SEM config. This issue clears automatically on the next successful command.

SEM believes this one is its own fault. If you can, open a bug report with the button on the notice — the form arrives already filled in. If you prefer, copy the context below into an email or forum post instead. Nothing is sent anywhere by this dialog.

```
{context}
```

Confirm to dismiss the notice.

confirm.title: Report this to SEM
confirm.description:
SEM has told **{name}** to stop, but no configured mechanism can actually open its contactor — so the car is still drawing {power} W. The only control SEM has for this charger is `{entity}`, whose minimum is above 0 A, so writing 0 A does nothing (SEM never writes a value the entity would reject). If you have a house battery this power is coming out of it, at any hour of the day or night. Fix: configure a start/stop switch entity (`ev_start_stop_entity`), a charge-mode entity, or a stop service for this charger in the SEM options. This issue clears as soon as the charger stops drawing.

SEM believes this one is its own fault. If you can, open a bug report with the button on the notice — the form arrives already filled in. If you prefer, copy the context below into an email or forum post instead. Nothing is sent anywhere by this dialog.

```
{context}
```

Confirm to dismiss the notice.

no_forecast_integration.title: No solar forecast integration detected
no_forecast_integration.description: SEM looked for a solar-forecast integration (Forecast.Solar, Solcast PV Solar, or a custom forecast sensor) for an hour after startup and didn't find one. Forecast-aware features (best-surplus-window tips, smart night charging, forecast dampening) are inactive until you install one. The issue clears automatically when SEM detects a forecast integration.

no_recorder.title: Recorder integration unavailable
no_recorder.description: SEM tried to bootstrap EV / charging history from the HA recorder but the read failed. EV intelligence (estimated SOC, daily decay) cannot warm-start without it; values populate slowly from live cycles instead. Usually a one-off transient — clears automatically on the next successful recorder read.

heat_pump_relay_unavailable.title: Heat pump SG-Ready {slot} unavailable
heat_pump_relay_unavailable.description: The configured SG-Ready relay entity `{entity_id}` ({slot}) has been unavailable/unknown for {minutes}+ minutes. SEM can register the heat pump controller fine, but every SG-Ready command will silently no-op until this entity reports a real state. Check the upstream device — ESP relay board, Shelly, Modbus-bridged template switch, or whichever integration owns this entity. The issue clears automatically when the relay next reports an on/off state.

heat_pump_partial_sg_ready.title: Heat pump SG-Ready half-configured
heat_pump_partial_sg_ready.description: Exactly one of the two SG-Ready relays (`heat_pump_relay1_entity` / `heat_pump_relay2_entity`) is set in SEM, with no climate-entity fallback. The SG-Ready protocol encodes the four states (BLOCKED / NORMAL / BOOST / FORCE_ON) as a 2-bit binary across BOTH relays, so a single relay cannot drive the protocol. Either configure the second relay too, or set a `heat_pump_climate_entity` to use the climate-only setpoint-boost path instead. The issue clears automatically once the config is valid.

hot_water_entity_unavailable.title: Hot water boiler control unavailable
hot_water_entity_unavailable.description: The configured hot-water control entity `{entity_id}` has been unavailable/unknown for {minutes}+ minutes. SEM can register the controller fine, but every surplus-dispatch command will silently no-op until the entity reports a real state. Check the upstream device — the boiler relay, water_heater integration, climate device, or whichever integration owns this entity. The issue clears automatically when the entity recovers.

hot_water_temperature_sensor_unavailable.title: Hot water temperature sensor unavailable
hot_water_temperature_sensor_unavailable.description: The configured hot-water temperature sensor `{entity_id}` has been unavailable/unknown for {minutes}+ minutes. SEM fails safe when this sensor is broken — the boiler is NOT activated on surplus until a real temperature reading returns, to avoid running the heater past its target without feedback. Check the sensor's upstream integration. The issue clears automatically when the sensor recovers.

confirm.title: Report this to SEM
confirm.description:
**{name}** is set to a percentage charge target, but your vehicle isn't reporting its state of charge right now, so SEM can't stop *exactly* at **{target}%**.

It isn't charging blind, though: from the last real reading this session it counts the energy actually delivered and stops once that measured total reaches your target — the overshoot is only what the car took since that reading. If no real reading has arrived at all this session (or SEM restarted mid-charge) there is nothing to count from, and charging runs until the car itself tapers near full.

For a cap that lands on the number, wire a **real vehicle SOC sensor** for this charger (Configuration → EV → Vehicle SOC entity). The battery % on the dashboard is SEM's *estimated* SOC, which it deliberately ignores for the hard limit (it can drift). This repair clears automatically as soon as a real SOC reading is available again.

SEM believes this one is its own fault. If you can, open a bug report with the button on the notice — the form arrives already filled in. If you prefer, copy the context below into an email or forum post instead. Nothing is sent anywhere by this dialog.

```
{context}
```

Confirm to dismiss the notice.

keba_failsafe_active.title: KEBA failsafe is enabled — disable it for steady charging
keba_failsafe_active.description:
Your KEBA charger "{name}" has its failsafe watchdog enabled. SEM (like evcc) no longer relies on it, but while it's on the charger keeps dropping the offered current to its 6 A fallback between commands, which makes charging oscillate (6↔9 A) and some cars (e.g. Renault Zoe) refuse to charge steadily.

Home Assistant's KEBA service can't switch it off (it won't accept a timeout of 0), so you need to disable it at the charger itself: set the **failsafe timeout to 0** (KEBA UDP `failsafe 0 0 1`, or via KEBA's KeContact tooling). See the linked guide for step-by-step instructions. This Repair clears automatically once the failsafe is off.

unmanaged_charger_found.title: SEM found a charger it is not managing
unmanaged_charger_found.description:
The device **{name}** looks like an EV charger, but no charger is configured in SEM — so SEM is leaving it alone ({count} candidate(s) found).

To let SEM optimise your charging with solar and cheap tariffs, add it under Settings → Devices & Services → SEM → Configure. That also unlocks the EV tab with the charge modes.

If this is not a car charger, ignore this notice — SEM will not control it either way.

lovelace_yaml_mode.title: Lovelace is in YAML mode — add SEM's card resources
lovelace_yaml_mode.description:
Your Home Assistant runs Lovelace in YAML mode, so SEM cannot register its dashboard cards automatically and the SEM dashboard shows "Configuration Error" cards.

Add this under `lovelace:` → `resources:` in your `configuration.yaml`, restart Home Assistant, then hard-refresh the browser (Ctrl+Shift+R):

```yaml
{resources}
```

This message disappears once the resources are loaded.

charger_control_entity_broken.title: EV charger control entity is not working: {name}
charger_control_entity_broken.description:
SEM is configured to use **`{entity_id}`** to {capability} on **{name}**, but that entity is `{reason}` — so every command SEM sends lands nowhere. SEM will still show a commanded current; the charger is not actually following it.

Common causes: the entity was renamed or removed upstream, or a template entity failed to load (a template `number` with an unsupported option loads only as `restored` and silently swallows writes).

Check the entity in **Developer Tools → States**. If it is missing or unavailable there, fix it at the source; if it is gone for good, re-point SEM under **Settings → Devices & Services → SEM → Configure → EV charger → Edit**.

battery_force_discharge_unsupported.title: Battery power setpoint cannot be written: {entity_id}
battery_force_discharge_unsupported.description:
SEM tried to write **{entity_id}** and the device refused every time: `{error}`.

The entity exists and SEM is addressing it correctly — the inverter's firmware simply does not implement writing that register. This usually means the entity you picked for *forcible discharge* in SEM's battery settings is readable but not writable on your hardware.

SEM has stopped trying, so this will no longer fill your log. Two things follow: the routine safety write SEM makes when returning the battery to normal operation is skipped (harmless — there was nothing set to clear), and **battery-to-grid export cannot run** on this battery. Charging, discharge limits and everyday operation are unaffected.

**If you do not use battery-to-grid export**, clear the forcible-discharge entity in SEM's battery settings and this notice goes away. **If you expected it to work**, the entity is likely the wrong one — or your inverter does not support commanded export. A restart makes SEM try again, so a firmware update or a corrected entity is picked up on its own.

charger_failsafe_suspected.title: Your wallbox undoes SEM's stop on a timer: {name}
charger_failsafe_suspected.description:
**{name}** re-enabled itself **{interval_s} seconds** after SEM stopped it — at least twice, with the same delay to the second, and with no command from SEM in between. That regularity is the signature of a charger-side **failsafe / controller-timeout fallback**, not of a car retrying.

SEM will not fight it: re-issuing stops faster would strobe the contactor and the box would win anyway. Until it is fixed the charger may draw at its stored fallback current (often 6 A) whenever SEM stops it.

**The fix is a one-time change on the wallbox itself.** Look for a failsafe or fallback-current setting in its configuration — on a KEBA these are `Curr FS` (fallback current) and `Tmo FS` (timeout) — and set the **fallback current to 0**, so a quiet controller means *stay off* rather than *charge at 6 A*. If your box is driven over Modbus, the setting usually lives in the same register block the integration already uses.

deye_system_work_mode_invalid.title: Deye export control cannot be used: {entity_id}
deye_system_work_mode_invalid.description: SEM cannot use {entity_id} for export control: {reason}. Check the select entity and the three option labels under Configuration → Battery intelligence.

battery_operating_mode_unexpected.title: Battery is in “{mode}” — SEM plans as if it were “{expected}”
battery_operating_mode_unexpected.description: The operating-mode selector {entity_id} reads “{mode}”. SEM's overnight model and the spendable budget assume “{expected}”; in other modes the inverter follows its own schedule underneath SEM and the plans may not hold. If this mode is deliberate, dismiss this — SEM will not fight your choice. Otherwise set the inverter back to “{expected}”.
